sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Southgate, Michigan?
sections.html:
Every Southgate house sale needs a Certificate of Compliance from the city, or a buyer who agrees in writing to take on the cited repairs. The Home Sales Department has run that program since July 12, 2021, and it applies to all residential dwellings, so it comes before your closing date.

Southgate is a Downriver suburb in Wayne County, about 14 miles southwest of downtown Detroit. The Census Bureau estimates 28,931 residents for July 2025, down from 30,014 in the 2020 census. Most owners can sell in one of three ways:

  • Listing with an agent, which brings the most buyers and the most steps, including the buyer's lender and appraisal.
  • Selling privately, where you set the price and manage the contract and the city inspection yourself.
  • Selling for cash to a buyer who takes the house as-is, with the buyer agreeing to assume any violations the city lists.

Read every offer for who pays the inspection fee, who handles repairs and when the money arrives.

sections.h2: How does the Southgate resale inspection work?
sections.html:
Southgate inspects the exterior of each residential dwelling before a sale. The city's Home Sales page says a Certificate of Compliance is valid for one sale or transfer, so a new inspection is needed each time the property changes hands.

  • The fee, effective June 1, 2024, is $200 and includes the initial inspection. Each additional inspection costs $60.
  • The owner can make every correction and obtain the certificate.
  • Or the owner can sell as-is. The buyer then signs an affidavit assuming the violations and an escrow agreement, and puts $1,000 in escrow before closing. The affidavit serves as the closing document.
  • Reports arrive by email, by mail or at pickup within 5 business days after the inspection.

The page advises having either the certificate or the buyer's signed affidavit in hand before you schedule the closing. The Home Sales office is a separate department from the Building Department. It sits in City Hall and answers at (734) 258-7783, so call that number rather than the building line when you have questions.

sections.h2: What is Southgate like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Southgate covers 6.875 square miles, all of it land, and it borders Riverview to the south, Wyandotte to the east, Allen Park to the northwest, Taylor to the west and Lincoln Park to the north, with Brownstown Charter Township to the southwest. The city was carved out of Ecorse Township and incorporated on October 8, 1958.

Before that the area was farmland and small settlements. Streets were platted in grids starting in the 1920s, though most building began after World War II, which tells you the age of the typical house. Local accounts say the name came from a shopping center planned at Eureka and Trenton roads and from the city's position as the south gate to Metro Detroit.

The population has been steady for decades. The census counted 30,136 residents in 2000, 30,047 in 2010 and 30,014 in 2020, so the city has changed little in size while the people living in it have aged: 19.5 percent are 65 or older in the Census estimate.

The retail figure reflects shopping and dining that draw people from neighboring Downriver cities. Wikipedia calls Southgate the dining capital of Downriver, and the city's commercial strips are part of why buyers see it as a convenient place to live.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads matter to Southgate buyers?
sections.html:
Southgate Community School District serves the city. Its public schools include Anderson High School, Davidson Middle School and elementary schools named Allen, Fordline, Grogan, North Pointe IB and Shelters. St. Pius X is a parochial school that opened in 1950, and Christ the King Lutheran is another private option.

Highway access is simple. I-75 crosses the northwest corner of the city, and M-85, known as Fort Street, forms most of the eastern boundary with Wyandotte. Four SMART bus routes pass through Southgate. The Southgate Civic Center has two ice rinks, and the Southgate Nature Center, a 30-acre preserve next to the high school, has ponds, a fishing dock and walking trails. Those amenities are worth a line in any listing or offer request.

sections.h2: What does a Southgate deed cost to record in Wayne County?
sections.html:
The Wayne County Register of Deeds charges $26 plus a $4 state survey and remonumentation fee, for $30 per document, under a fee schedule that took effect January 1, 2026. The office says this was its first fee increase since 1996.

Transfer tax is due at recording unless a proper exemption is noted. The Register of Deeds prints the county rate as $0.55 per $500 and the state rate as $3.75 per $500, or $8.60 per $1000 of the consideration amount.

  • Warranty deeds, deeds with a covenant of warranty and land contracts must be certified for taxes by the Wayne County Treasurer before recording.
  • The office takes cash, check or money order for transfer tax and accepts debit and credit cards with matching ID, though not American Express or Discover.
  • Personal checks are accepted by mail but not at the counter, and each document needs its own check.
  • The office takes documents in person or by mail and can be reached at (313) 224-5851.

After closing, Michigan Treasury guidance says the buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit, Form 2766, with the local assessor within 45 days of a transfer, citing MCL 211.27a(10).

sections.h2: What if my Southgate house is a rental?
sections.html:
The city also runs a separate multi-family rental certification and inspection program with its own page, and rental owners should read it before listing a building. Ask the Building Department whether your property falls under that program, and ask the Home Sales office whether the same sale also needs a Certificate of Compliance.

A tenant in the house complicates the exterior inspection less than an interior one, but you still need to coordinate dates, and a cash buyer who plans to keep the tenant will ask for the lease, the deposit amount and the rent roll. Have those ready before you ask for offers.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Compliance to sell in Southgate?
faqs.a: Yes, for residential dwellings sold since July 12, 2021. You can fix the items the city cites, or sell as-is if the buyer signs an affidavit and escrow agreement and puts $1,000 in escrow before closing.

faqs.q: How much is the Southgate resale inspection?
faqs.a: The city lists $200 for the initial inspection, effective June 1, 2024, and $60 for each additional inspection. Check the Home Sales page for any change before you book.

faqs.q: How long does a Southgate Certificate of Compliance last?
faqs.a: It is valid for one sale or transfer of the dwelling. A new inspection is required each time the house is sold or transferred again.

faqs.q: What does Wayne County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds lists $30 per document, made up of $26 plus a $4 state survey and remonumentation fee, under a schedule that took effect January 1, 2026. Transfer tax is separate and is paid at recording.

faqs.q: Can a cash buyer close without the city repairs finished?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer signs the affidavit assuming the violations and puts $1,000 in escrow before closing, and that affidavit serves as the closing document. Confirm the escrow terms in your purchase agreement.
